headline: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff
dek: According to Wired and the Guardian, the CEO spoke at his first all-hands since returning.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The apology
body: Jensen Huang apologized to employees and admitted violating the code of conduct (Wired AI, The Guardian Technology).
He cited serious personal mistakes that hurt his family, according to Wired AI.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: What else he said
s3.body: The meeting also covered politics and succession, per the sources.

points.t: Huang denied Trump pressured the board (The Guardian Technology).
He said he is in therapy and it has helped (Wired AI, CNBC Technology).
He said Nvidia already has many capable leaders (CNBC Technology).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: For TechCrunch AI, the bigger risk for Huang is cultural, not legal.
Staff may feel embarrassed even without formal punishment (TechCrunch AI).

items.t: Internal trust is the pressure point, says TechCrunch AI.
Huang says the board made the reinstatement call (Wired AI).
Nvidia did not comment on the meeting (The Guardian Technology, CNBC Technology).

caption.hook: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff at his first all-hands since returning as CEO.
body: According to Wired and the Guardian, the executive admitted violating the company's code of conduct and described serious personal mistakes. CNBC, which spoke to people in the room, confirms the tone of the apology and says he mentioned going to therapy.

Huang also denied that Trump pressured the board to bring him back and called the formal succession process flawed (Wired AI). TechCrunch argues the bigger risk is cultural: employees may feel embarrassed even without formal punishment. Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment. The full story is at the link in bio.
